_comment: The part shops on their own map (drawn on the dealer map picture, without the car lots). The save keeps a shop's business (open, closing down, closed, waiting to open),
its stock and what the player has spent there; everything else is read from here and merged over the save, so a
field added here reaches every existing save.
kind: specialist (new parts for its makes: every part pack whose "make" is one of them, a mod's too), speed (new
performance parts for any make, or its makes: carburettors, blowers, cams, manifolds, heads, headers, nitrous, none
a car came with), wheels (new tyres, rims, brakes, springs and shocks) or junkyard (used parts and whole engines out
of wrecks; buys the player's old parts for more than a trade-in). groups narrows a shop to kinds of part as the
mapX/mapY are fractions of the dealer map picture, as the dealers' are (see dealers/dealers.json); keep a pin
about 0.055 across or 0.035 down from any other shop's, or the name plates overlap.
priceFactor (against the list price; a junkyard's against what the used part is worth), buyFactor (what it pays
for a part, against its worth), stockLow/stockHigh (how many different parts; a junkyard: parts in the yard) and
restockDays are optional: left out, the kind's own (PartShopRules).
startsOpen false: not in business when a game starts; it opens some day, as the dealers do. About 60% of the
shops are open at a time, and now and then one goes out of business with a closing-down sale.

shops.name: Hemi Hut
shops.blurb: Nothing but Mopar, from a slant six gasket to a race Hemi. They know what you drive before you park it.

shops.name: Blue Oval Parts
shops.blurb: Ford parts, sixes and eights, on shelves that go back further than you can see.

shops.name: Bowtie Supply
shops.blurb: General Motors parts counter. If Detroit cast it, they have one out back or can get one by Friday.

shops.name: Bellflower Speed & Custom
shops.blurb: Carburettors, blowers, cams and headers, for anything with pistons. Not much of each, and not cheap.

shops.name: South Bay Speed
shops.blurb: A speed shop by the beach, run by somebody who builds dragsters on weekends. The good stuff goes fast.

shops.name: Foothill Tire & Brake
shops.blurb: Tyres, wheels, brakes, springs and shocks. Cheaper than the catalogue, and you drive it home today.

shops.name: Inland Tire & Brake
shops.blurb: A big tyre barn out past the vineyards. Stacks of rubber, and brakes for anything.

shops.name: San Pedro Auto Wreckers
shops.blurb: Acres of wrecks by the docks. Bring your own tools, and haggle: nothing here has a price tag.

shops.name: Sun Valley Salvage
shops.blurb: The valley's scrapyard, where the freeway wrecks end up. Whole engines, if you get there first.

shops.name: Fontana Wrecking
shops.blurb: A long way out, and the cheapest yard in the county. The dogs are friendly. Mostly.
